identity.industry: Financial Services — NBFC (digital/co-lending + own retail lending app "Apollo Cash")

summary.oneLiner: Apollo Finvest is a small NBFC in transition: it is deliberately shrinking its legacy term-loan-to-NBFC book (causing a slight YoY dip in FY26 revenue/PAT/AUM) in favour of (a) safer "warehouse"-structured lending with escrow control and (b) its newly launched own-book retail app "Apollo Cash," which targets first-time-credit / blue-collar / gig-worker borrowers using a device-signal-heavy underwriting model rather than bureau/banking data. Apollo Cash is very early (~3 months live) but growing ~300% MoM in disbursements with zero paid marketing.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- Single standalone entity — no subsidiaries or segment reporting disclosed on this call.
- Book composition described qualitatively: term loans (legacy, shrinking), warehouse-structured loans (~27% of term book), co-lending/BC partnerships (scaling), Apollo Cash (new, small but fast-growing).

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline (loan book & pipeline)
order_book.body:
- No disclosed rupee book size. Key mix data point: retail book was 24% of AUM in the prior year, now 50-51% of AUM this quarter — the single biggest disclosed change this call.
- Apollo Cash: live in ~19,000 PIN codes across India (pan-India digital reach); ~75,000+ applications and ~18,000+ loans disbursed since launch; cumulative disbursement >INR 5 cr; monthly disbursement trajectory: Feb ~INR 30 lakh → Mar ~INR 1.2 cr (+300% MoM) → Apr ~INR 3 cr.
- Co-lending: partners now "iron[ed] out" operational issues and gained confidence in book quality after a long integration period; management expects visible scale-up with these partners "in this coming quarter."

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Loan-book mix, next ~8 months:** Apollo Cash ~20-25% of book; term loans ~40% (being actively converted into warehouse structures); balance = co-lending/BC partnerships.
- **Loan-book mix, next ~12-24 months:** retail exposure (Apollo Cash + partnerships) to become "vast majority" of book; warehousing/term-loan share to keep shrinking. Longer-term (~2-year horizon) target: Apollo Cash ~50-60% of book.
- **Apollo Cash "Year 1" targets:** total disbursements ~INR 50 cr; resulting AUM ~INR 10-15 cr (book churns quickly, so AUM << cumulative disbursements); Apollo Cash to be ~15-20% of total loan book by year-end.
- **Capital raise:** no external fundraising planned this financial year — management cites low debt-to-equity.
- **Warehouse conversion:** ~27% of term-loan book currently in warehouse structure (up from near-zero); management wants to keep raising this, ideally phasing out plain term loans entirely — no explicit target date given.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Apollo Cash is the core growth optionality**: management explicitly frames it as "the largest opportunity" in the company's 8-9 year history, sizing the addressable opportunity at "almost close to 50 to 100x" the business built to date. Entirely unquantified/aspirational at this stage — treat as high-conviction management belief, not disclosed TAM data.
- Underwriting model (device/behavioral signals) is being positioned as reusable infrastructure that could scale well beyond the current ~3-month-old book.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- Impairment/provisioning on loans declined YoY — a function of book mix (term loans still dominant in FY26, carrying more conservative/lower provisioning than the shorter-tenure, higher-delinquency retail book). Management explicitly flagged this trend will change (i.e., impairment likely rises) as the retail book share increases — an important item to watch next quarter.
- Apollo Cash customer acquisition cost currently ~zero (no paid marketing) — not guided to stay at zero as scale increases.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- No fundraising planned this financial year; management cites low debt-to-equity as the reason external capital is not currently being pursued.
- No dividend/buyback commentary on this call.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body:
- Candid: proactively disclosed a YoY dip in revenue/PAT/AUM and openly flagged that the currently favorable (lower) impairment trend will reverse as mix shifts — not spun as purely positive.
- Highly promotional/confident language on Apollo Cash's opportunity size ("50 to 100x," "top 1%," "massive opportunity") without corresponding disclosed unit economics (loss rates, yields, cost of funds) — enthusiasm outpaces disclosed evidence at this early stage.
- CEO answered a candid, somewhat adversarial analyst question (would a prime, well-banked 25-year-old get approved?) directly and specifically ("most likely end up getting rejected") — signals genuine underwriting-model discipline rather than growth-at-any-cost.

moat.title: 6a. Moat & competitive position
moat.body:
- **Data/underwriting moat**: management argues that continuously gathering borrower behavioral signals (device intelligence, SMS patterns, app usage, location/e-commerce order history) compounds over time and cannot be "caught up" on retroactively — a competitor starting later cannot backfill the historical data. Quote: "it will be very, very difficult for another company to build this... because of the data, because of the moat, because of the insights that you can only get by doing this."
- **Brand/CAC moat (evidenced, not aspirational)**: Apollo Cash has acquired 1 lakh+ downloads and ~75,000+ applications with **zero paid marketing spend**; management attributes this to 8-9 years of borrower-side brand recognition built through the earlier NBFC/co-lending business — organic ~1,000-2,000 daily downloads driven by branded search, not performance marketing. This is a concrete, quantified evidence point (unlike the data-moat claim, which is asserted but not evidenced with metrics).

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- Impairment/delinquency trend is set to worsen (management's own admission) as the higher-delinquency retail/Apollo Cash book displaces the lower-delinquency term-loan book — watch loss-rate disclosures next 1-2 quarters.
- Apollo Cash is ~3 months old with no seasoned delinquency data yet (first repayment cohorts have not been through a full cycle) — asset-quality performance is unproven.
- Underwriting model targets thin-file/underbanked/blue-collar borrowers explicitly — a segment historically prone to higher default risk industry-wide; management itself notes NBFCs "go bust" lending into this space via weaker models.
- Continued dependence on co-lending partner integration pace — scale-up timing is partner-controlled, not fully in Apollo's hands.
- No hard revenue/PAT/AUM numbers or growth rates disclosed verbally — limits ability to independently size the "slight dip" or verify guidance against a base.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- Underwriting explicitly uses non-traditional behavioral data — e.g., a borrower's Swiggy/Zomato/Amazon delivery order history is cited as a **better address-verification signal than KYC documents**. Bureau + banking data are described as only ~10% of the underwriting decision; the remaining ~90% comes from device/behavioral signals (reported ~10,000+ variables extracted per phone).
- The underwriting model is deliberately designed to **reject** well-banked, prime borrowers as anomalous/fraud-like, because such a profile doesn't match the target "Bharat" (blue-collar/gig-worker/first-time-credit) customer base — a self-selecting funnel by design, not an oversight.
- Retention strategy for repeat borrowers is a three-lever "trust escalator": lower pricing, higher loan quantum, and much faster re-application UX (first loan >10 screens vs. ~3 clicks / under 5 seconds for a repeat borrower).
- App is English-only by design choice but automatically renders in the device's OS-set language (e.g., Hindi) with no dedicated localization build; collections communication is sent in the borrower's stated preferred language.

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)
qoq_log.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (this):** FY26 revenue/PAT/AUM slightly down YoY (unquantified) on deliberate term-loan wind-down; retail book jumped from 24% → 50-51% of AUM; warehouse structure now ~27% of term-loan book; Apollo Cash launched (~3 months live), disbursements ramping ~300% MoM (Feb ~30L → Mar ~1.2cr → Apr ~3cr), 19,000 PIN codes, 1L+ downloads, zero paid marketing; guided Apollo Cash Year-1 disbursements ~INR 50cr / AUM ~INR 10-15cr / ~15-20% of book; no fundraise planned this FY.
- **Q1 FY27 → check:** Has Apollo Cash disbursement momentum (300% MoM growth) continued or decelerated? Has impairment/delinquency started rising as retail mix grows (management's own flagged risk)? Loan-book mix vs. the "8-month" guided split (Apollo Cash ~20-25% / term loans ~40% / balance partnerships)? Any hard revenue/PAT/AUM figures now disclosed to size the FY26 "slight dip"? Co-lending partner scale-up materializing as promised "this coming quarter"?
